threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the 38' instead of just '38'. Locals don’t bother with ‘the’—it’s all about speed when you’re waiting for a bus.
Caught a guy on the 59 last night trying to barter a half-eaten pasty for a bus ticket. Driver just shook his head and laughed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a toddler gleefully feeding the pigeons a leftover döner in Hermannplatz, I realized this was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a dog park with a bar serving craft beer right next to it. The pups roam free while their humans sip ales. Perfect combo.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their ability to navigate BART delays, but a newbie stares blankly at the schedule app like it's hieroglyphics.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus that had to stop because a guy was arguing with a pigeon. That pigeon stood its ground. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists miss that the best local bars close early, thinking they’ll find a late-night vibe like in tourist traps. It’s the locals' time to unwind.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still frown at the late-night noise; locals just shrug and carry on. It's like an unwritten rule here.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can tell a newbie by how they still struggle to differentiate between the 30 bus and the 149. Regulars know which one to catch at night.
Last night on the N35, a bloke started singing opera loudly. Half the bus joined in. Never thought I'd see that at 2 AM in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard the old Turkish shopkeeper gossiping about the latest BVG strikes at the corner café, while the kids played football right in the street.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night Döner stand that doubles as an art gallery, showcasing local artists while you wait for your kebab.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they react when BART delays hit—no complaints, just a resigned chuckle about the inevitable chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 today, driver stopped mid-ride to explain to a guy why he can’t bring his skateboard on. Classic Tenderloin moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas. In Gràcia, you’ll find places dishing out hearty platillos that are anything but typical.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still call it ‘La Rambla’ with the emphasis on the 'la,' not realizing it’s just ‘Rambla’ to the locals.
